The picks

Chosen for the recipient and use described, using published product information. We have not hands-on tested these products.

  1. 1. Airport-radio listeners and plane spotters

    ATC — Live Air Traffic Radio

    Our app: Pilot Gift Guide is produced by the team behind ATC. This is a recommendation of our own product.

    You do not have to be a pilot to enjoy hearing airport activity. ATC pairs live airport audio with maps and transcripts on iPhone, giving an aviation enthusiast several ways to follow along. Start by checking whether the airports they are interested in are covered and whether they would use a subscription.

    Live airport audio with aircraft maps, transcripts and replay in one iPhone app.

    Keep in mind
    Coverage varies by airport; a subscription is not automatically transferable as a gift.
    Before you choose
    iPhone with iOS 18 or later; check airport coverage and current plans.
    Subscription; see current plans at ATC ↗Listed 2026-10-21
    Official App Store details ↗

    An evening project that becomes a permanent part of their aviation corner. A strong choice for someone who loves airliners as much as flying them.

    Keep in mind
    The long finished model needs substantial display space, and an adult building kit is not a quick activity.
    Before you choose
    Allow a long display shelf: the finished model measures 41.5 inches. Ages 18+.

Find their kind of aviation

Airliner enthusiasts, general aviation fans and military airshow followers can have very different tastes. Look at the aircraft they photograph or the stories they share. Someone who follows long-haul airlines may love Concorde but have little connection to a Cessna. A Blue Angels fan may appreciate an ornament of that team more than a generic airplane decoration. Make the category personal before choosing the product.

For the builder

LEGO’s Concorde is an adult building project and a display piece in one. The official listing specifies 2,083 pieces and an age recommendation of 18+. That makes it a better fit for someone who enjoys a detailed build than someone who wants a small ready-made object. The display footprint matters: measure the shelf rather than judging scale from product photographs. Leave time to build it, too; the project itself is part of the gift.

For the collector

A finished aircraft model is an alternative when building is not the attraction. The Cessna 172 mahogany model is a starting point for someone connected to light aircraft, especially if the type appears in their own flying memories. Check size, material and stand details at the retailer. Collectors may care about exact variants and liveries, so an apparently small detail can determine whether the model fits their collection.

For everyday enthusiasm

A cap, shirt or holiday ornament lets someone enjoy the interest without dedicating a shelf to it. Match the aircraft brand or display team to the person. A framed photo from an airshow you attended together can be even more personal. Choose the image, print size and frame around a real memory rather than a generic airplane slogan.

Keep technical gifts off the surprise list

An enthusiast does not necessarily need an aviation headset, kneeboard or flight training equipment. Those are specialized tools. Unless the recipient has asked for them, use the budget on a gift related to the part of aviation they already enjoy. If they are considering learning to fly, a conversation with a local flight school can help you explore an introductory experience and its booking terms.

Prices and availability can change. Check the exact model, delivered total and return terms with the seller. Our recommendations are researched editorial selections, not hands-on test results.
